text:
support_agent_ella: Hey team, incoming escalation from Acme Inc — they report intermittent 502/504 + request timeouts for hosted inference in the past ~30m. Tenant: acme-inc. Sample request id: req_0a1b2c. Model: redwood/open-7b-v2. Observed p95 token latency ~8s and a bunch of gateway 504s. They mentioned a sudden traffic spike from their side (concurrency ~25) and long prompts (~1200 tokens). Can we triage? :eyes:

oncall_mike: Ack — looking. Can you paste the top trace IDs and any ingress/gateway logs? Also what region/cluster?

support_agent_ella: Region: us-west-2 (hosted). Attached traces in ticket: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/7890 (internal). Quick repro we got from customer:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-7b-v2","input":"<~1200-token prompt>","max_tokens":512,"concurrency":20}'
```
They also sent a sequence of 30k requests over a 2min burst.

opsbot: [Alert] gateway.request_504_rate (us-west-2) spiked to 3.8% in last 15m. Average queue_depth increased from ~30 to 220.

eng_zhou: Thanks. Initial hypothesis: request queue saturation -> continuous-batching backlog -> dequeue timeouts for tail requests. Need the batcher metrics and gateway request-queue logs. Check metrics: `batcher.queue_depth`, `batcher.pending_tokens`, `gateway.enqueue_rejections`, `router.backpressure_events`.

eng_zhou: Can someone run: 
```bash
# fetch gateway logs for the request id
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n hosted --since=1h | grep req_0a1b2c -A 8 -B 2
# query batcher queue depth around spike
curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=batcher.queue_depth&tenant=acme-inc&range=15m"
```

sre_lucy: Pasting relevant gateway snippet from host-gw-3: 
```
[2026-02-12T14:22:07Z] RequestQueue.enq req=req_0a1b2c depth=238
[2026-02-12T14:22:07Z] Batcher.dequeue start batch_size=16 tokens_in_batch=18400
[2026-02-12T14:22:08Z] Batcher.dequeue timed out after 300ms; pending_batches=4
[2026-02-12T14:22:09Z] RequestQueue.dequeue timeout req=req_0a1b2c wait=310ms -> gateway 504
```
Looks like the queue depth approached the soft limit and dequeue latencies were high; batcher blocked on a few large sequences.

eng_zhou: That log matches continuous-batching backlog. Two quick mitigations we can apply while we investigate: 
- temporarily lower `batcher.max_batch_size` from 32 -> 8 for the hosted gateway pool handling acme-inc (reduces batch assembly wait)
- set `gateway.early_reject.threshold` to 180 (early reject requests when depth > threshold) to avoid long tail 504s
Both are config toggles that we can roll with a short canary.

support_agent_ella: I'll ask Acme if they can throttle back for ~10m while we put mitigations. Also offering them temporary credits.

customer_success_raj: Please do offer credits and let them know we're prioritizing — ping me when mitigations are in. :thumbsup:

eng_zhou: I can push the config to staging now. Planned steps: 
1) push `batcher.max_batch_size=8` to staging for the pool; watch `p95_token_latency` and `enq_rate` for 5m.
2) if stable, roll to prod for the specific cluster.
3) if still bad, route acme-inc to fallback model `redwood/open-3b-v1` or to dedicated pool if they have a reservation.

oncall_mike: Go ahead. Assigning incident #INC-2026-045. eskalation:eng-team. Keep notes in the ticket.

eng_zhou: Devops push done to staging at 14:27 UTC. Monitoring: https://dashboards.internal/d/ingress/hosted-gateway?var-tenant=acme-inc. Staging p95 token latency dropped from 8.1s -> 2.3s for a simulated burst.

sre_lucy: After prod roll at 14:33 UTC we saw queue depth fall to ~40 and 504s drop to near zero. Still seeing a handful of slow tail requests correlated with >2000-token prompts.

support_agent_ella: I told Acme we rolled a mitigation and asked them to try their burst again in 10m; they confirmed a lower failure rate but one reproed 504 with req id req_7d2e9f.

eng_zhou: For root cause: likely combination of very large prompts (tokens per request high) + sudden concurrency spike -> batcher assembled very large token batches causing long GPU exec times and head-of-line blocking for short requests. Long-term actions: 
- partition long-seq requests into a separate pool (sequence-length routing)
- add tenant priority and admission control to protect short requests
- increase `batcher.dequeue_timeout_ms` tuning and implement preemptive slicing for huge sequences
- update runbook with exact thresholds and quick rollback steps

customer_success_raj: Can we add a proactive alert tied to `batcher.pending_tokens` so we auto-notify before 504s hit customer? Acme would appreciate heads up.

oncall_mike: Good idea. Can we also add automated fallback routing to smaller model for tenants without dedicated capacity? eng_zhou?

eng_zhou: Yes, add to roadmap. For now I'll create a short doc with repro steps and the config diffs we applied and attach to the ticket.

support_agent_ella: Putting final status in ticket: partially mitigated by lowering batch size + early reject; customer seeing improved success rate. Follow-ups: permanent routing change + runbook updates + credit offer. Closing Slack thread and moving postmortem to #postmortems after runbook items are captured.

oncall_mike: Thanks all. Closing here — transfer to postmortems for writeup. :white_check_mark:
